'Green Bench' (a bench hearing environment-related matters): the term appears in neither the Constitution text nor the NCERT Judiciary chapter used as sources. Source gap; not taught in this chapter.

The Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha enjoys the rank of a High Court Judge: the question is about the Leader of the Opposition's rank (Parliament, POL-09/POL-10 territory); a High Court Judge appears only as an option. Not this chapter's subject.

POL-13.note: Governor of a State is appointed by the President (Art 155; Constitution p. 70). Taught in appointment_term and in question q05.
A state legislature's Bill becomes an Act when the Governor assents to it (Art 200; Constitution p. 91). Taught in legislative_powers and in question q21.
Executive power of the State is vested in the Governor by Article 154 (Constitution p. 70). Taught in governor_intro and in question q02.

Pardoning power is enjoyed by the President (Art 72) and the Governor (Art 161; Constitution p. 72). This chapter teaches the Governor's Art 161 power and its scope; the President's Art 72 is POL-07's ground. Taught in ordinance_pardon.

District Judges are appointed by the Governor in consultation with the High Court (Art 233; Constitution p. 109). Taught in appointments_misc and in question q37. Subordinate judiciary detail is POL-12's ground.

Members of a State Public Service Commission are appointed by the Governor (Art 316; Constitution p. 177); removal only by the President (Art 317). Taught in appointments_misc and in questions q38-q39.
The Advocate General of a State is appointed by the Governor (Art 165; Constitution p. 74). Taught in appointments_misc and in question q36.

Time-anchored current-affairs item: who was Governor of Jammu & Kashmir at the time of the January 2020 exam (Satya Pal Malik). A person's name/tenure is not in the constitutional or NCERT sources used for this chapter, and it is not a constitutional-provision question; not taught.

POL-14.note: The upper House of the State Legislature is called the Vidhan Parishad (bank key D). Taught in the kathamo section from Article 168(2) (claim c19) and mirrored in practice question q02.

A bill of a state legislature becomes an Act when the Governor signs (assents to) it (bank key B). Taught in the odhibeshon_aain section from Article 200 (claim c66) and mirrored in practice question q40.

First woman Chief Minister of India (Sucheta Kripalani, bank key C): the fact appears in none of this chapter's fetched sources (Constitution text, NCERT Executive/Legislature chapters, WB Assembly site), so it is not taught here. Source gap, disclosed in REPORT.md.

Which amendment relates to SC/ST reservation and Anglo-Indian representation in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies (bank key D, 79th Amendment): an amendments-chapter question (primary POL-06); State Assemblies are mentioned only as part of the amendment's subject. Not this chapter's scope.

POL-15.note: Concurrent List subjects: the chapter teaches the original 47 numbered entries and the present 52 after the 42nd Amendment insertions (claims c13, c14); exam_note in talika_bonton gives the 2016 key (47) and the current count. Mirrored in the chapter's teaching, not as a practice item.

'Neither purely federal nor purely unitary but a combination of both' attributed to D. D. Basu: the attribution appears in neither the Constitution text nor any source fetched for this chapter (the NCERT Federalism chapter could not be fetched this run). Source gap; the chapter teaches the mixed federal-unitary character only from the constitutional text (Arts. 1-4, 248, 368 proviso) without naming the quote or its author.
Same D. D. Basu attribution as WBCS 2016 Q44 (K. C. Wheare's 'quasi-federal' is also named in the bank explanation): not in the fetched sources. Source gap; not taught.
Seventh Schedule distributes power between the Union and the States (claims c50, c06). Taught in talika_bonton and tofoshil; remember box in talika_bonton cites this very question.
Inter-State Council is established by the President by order under Article 263 (claim c28). Taught in proshasonik; exam_note cites this question; mirrored in practice question q20.
Education is in the Concurrent List (List III entry 25, claims c12, c13). Taught in talika_bonton; mirrored in practice question q11.

Anti-defection law = 52nd Amendment, 1985, which added the Tenth Schedule (claim c53). Taught in tofoshil; exam_note cites this question; mirrored in practice question q39. Detail of the Tenth Schedule is POL-17's scope.
GST Council is headed by the Union Finance Minister as Chairperson under Article 279A(2) (claim c40). Taught in gst_artho; exam_note cites this question; mirrored in practice question q32.
Article 1 defines the name and territory of the Union ('India, that is Bharat, shall be a Union of States', claim c01). Taught in juktorashtro; exam_note cites this question.
Article 280 lays down the Finance Commission (claim c43). Taught in gst_artho at the level this chapter owns (constitution, composition, duties); the Commission's detailed working is POL-18's scope.

Finance Commission = a Chairperson and four other members, Article 280(1) (claim c43). Taught in gst_artho; remember box cites this question; mirrored in practice question q33. Primary chapter POL-18, but the composition is taught here.

President's duty to lay documents before Parliament (Finance Commission recommendations, UPSC report, CAG report, SC/ST Commission reports): only the Finance Commission limb is taught here (Article 281, claim c45). The full question spans POL-11/POL-18 territory and is not answerable from this chapter alone.
'How many Finance Commissions have submitted reports so far?' (keyed 12 in 2016): a time-varying count that appears in no fetched source and changes with each Commission. Not taught; POL-18's scope.

Statement item pairing the Finance Commission (constitutional) with the National Commission for Women (statutory): the FC's constitutional basis (Article 280) is taught here, but the NCW's statutory status is in no fetched source and belongs to POL-19. Not taught as a whole.
Article for President's Rule in a State (356): emergency provisions are POL-16's chapter; this chapter covers legislative/administrative/financial relations only. Not taught here.
President's Rule Article (356): POL-16 (emergency). Not taught here.
'The President of India can declare' (national/constitutional/financial emergency): emergency types are POL-16's scope. Not taught here.

'Which one is not a Union Territory?' (Tripura): the chapter teaches that the First Schedule has two parts, the States and the Union territories (claim c48), but the fetched quotes do not reproduce the individual State/UT lists, so Tripura's status as a State is not established from this chapter's claims. Not taught.

State exempted from SC reservation in Panchayati Raj institutions: a Part IX / Article 243D-243M question owned by POL-20; the Eleventh Schedule is taught here only as a schedule entry. Not taught here.

POL-16.note: 44th Amendment made written Cabinet advice mandatory for an Emergency declaration (Article 352(3)); taught in national_emergency standard text and question q11. Cross-listed as untaught in the POL-02/POL-04/POL-08/POL-11 maps with 'belongs to POL-16' — now taught here.

Articles 20 and 21 cannot be suspended under Article 359 during a National Emergency; taught in effects_and_rights standard text (with the exact PYQ flagged) and question q15. Cross-listed as untaught in the POL-03/POL-04 maps with 'belongs to POL-16' — now taught here.

The President can declare a National Emergency, a Constitutional (President's Rule) Emergency and a Financial Emergency; taught in emergency_overview (three categories, all proclaimed by the President) and question q02. Note: the bank item's keyed option is 'All of the above'; the chapter teaches the underlying fact, and its own practice questions avoid that banned option format.
The power to declare an Emergency lies with the President; taught in emergency_overview (exam_note box reproduces this Clerkship question) and question q02.
President's Rule is promulgated under Article 356; taught in presidents_rule standard text (with the exact PYQ flagged) and question q04.

POL-17.note: Taught: the voting age was reduced from 21 years to 18 years in the 1980s by the 61st Amendment, 1988 (w.e.f. 28-3-1989).
Taught: the right to vote and to be elected is a Constitutional Right, flowing from Article 326 (adult suffrage), not a Fundamental Right.
Taught: the Election Commission is constituted by the President under Article 324.
Taught: the anti-defection law (Tenth Schedule) was added by the 52nd Amendment, 1985.

Not taught here: members of the Public Accounts Committee are elected by members of both Houses through proportional representation by single transferable vote — belongs to POL-09/10 (parliamentary committees).
Not taught here: the Vice-President is elected by an electoral college of members of both Houses of Parliament (Article 66) — belongs to POL-07.

Not taught here: the question asks which match is incorrect — Finance Commission with Article 324. The chapter teaches that Article 324 is the Election Commission, but the Finance Commission's own article (280) is POL-18, so the full match-question is not taught here.
Not taught here: asks what the SVEEP programme is (full form: Systematic Voters' Education and Electoral Participation) — no verified GOVT source in hand, so it is not covered in this chapter.

POL-18.note: 'How many Finance Commissions have submitted reports so far?' (keyed: Twelve). Not taught: the count is time-bound and changes with every five-year cycle; the chapter teaches the Article 280 cycle and composition, and no fetched source used for this chapter states a running count of commissions.
Taught: the Finance Commission consists of a Chairman and four other members, all appointed by the President (Art 280(1), claim c19); also an exam_note box in the section.

Partly covered only: this chapter teaches that Finance Commission recommendations (Art 281, c24) and CAG reports (Art 151, c30) are laid before Parliament by the President, and the CAG section's deep text uses this very chain. But the keyed answer also requires the National Commission for Scheduled Castes report (Art 338), which belongs to POL-19, so the full key is not derivable from this chapter alone.

Not taught: the Public Accounts Committee's size, remit and working belong to POL-10 (parliamentary procedure). Only statement 3 (PAC examines the CAG's report) touches this chapter's subject; the chapter does not teach PAC composition or functions.
Taught: Article 280 lays down the Finance Commission (claim c19); the section's exam_note box names this exact article-body pairing.
Taught: members of a State Public Service Commission are appointed by the Governor of the State (Art 316(1), claim c04).
Not taught: the Chairman of the Public Accounts Committee being from the Opposition is a parliamentary-committee convention belonging to POL-10; this chapter covers the CAG, not the PAC.

Not taught: 'a Public Service Commission was first established by the Government of India Act, 1919' is pre-constitutional legislative history (HIS-27 scope). This chapter teaches only the constitutional scheme of Articles 315-323; none of the sources fetched for it covers the 1919 Act.

Taught: the Finance Commission is a constitutional body because Article 280 itself creates it (claim c19), and the section's dont_confuse box teaches the constitutional-vs-statutory distinction the question tests. The National Commission for Women limb (a statutory body) is POL-19's subject in detail.
Taught: the Attorney General for India is appointed by the President (Art 76(1), claim c32); the section's standard text names this exact exam point.

POL-19.note: NITI Aayog is set up by a resolution of the Union Cabinet — taught verbatim (PIB release on the Cabinet Resolution: 'The Government has replaced Planning Commission with a new institution named NITI Aayog... A cabinet Resolution issued today gave details'). Practice q41 mirrors it.
Same question as WBCS 2016 Q176 (NITI Aayog set up by a Union Cabinet resolution); taught in niti_aayog and q41.
Ombudsman institution originated in Sweden — taught from the Maharashtra Lokayukta official site ('The office of Ombudsman has been in existence in Sweden since 1809'); lokpal section and exam q39.

What the second meeting of the NITI Aayog Governing Council emphasised is a dated current-affairs detail (land pooling / cooperative federalism discussion of 2015). The chapter teaches the Governing Council's composition, not the agenda of a specific meeting; no fetched official source used here records that meeting's emphasis.

The Constitution (123rd Amendment) Bill, 2017 empowers the National Commission for Backward Classes — taught as the enacted result: Article 338B inserted by the 102nd Amendment, 2018 (w.e.f. 15-8-2018); jatiya_commission section, exam_note in text and q17.

The Protection of Human Rights Act was passed in 1993 — taught (Act deemed in force 28 September 1993, s.1(3)); nhrc_gathon exam_note warns against the '10 of 1994' Act-number trap. Also mapped in POL-04.

NITI Aayog's North-East Region District SDG Index was released with UNDP support — a current-affairs partnership detail. The chapter teaches NITI Aayog's structure and objectives only; the UNDP partnership for that index is not in the fetched official sources used.

Statements: (I) Finance Commission is a Constitutional Body (POL-18); (II) National Commission for Women is a Statutory Body — taught here: NCW is constituted under s.3 of the National Commission for Women Act, 1990 (PHRA s.2(j) definition quoted). Keyed answer 'Both (I) and (II)' follows.

Year the Planning Commission was established (keyed 1950). The chapter teaches only that NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission by Cabinet Resolution (PIB release, which gives no 1950 date); the Planning Commission's own 1950 resolution was not among the fetched sources, so the year is not taught. Source gap, disclosed.

Headquarters of the UN Human Rights Council (Geneva) — an international-organisations GK question, not India's NHRC. This chapter teaches the Indian statutory NHRC (HQ Delhi, PHRA s.3(5)); the UN body is out of scope.

POL-20.note: Which Article desires the organisation of village panchayats? Art 40 (Directive Principles); chapter teaches Art 40 in section why_local.
Which article describes the organisation of village panchayats? Art 40; chapter teaches Art 40 in section why_local.
The Panchayati Raj system has three tiers; chapter teaches the village, intermediate and district levels (Art 243B) in section three_tiers.
The Panchayati Raj system has three tiers; chapter teaches the village, intermediate and district levels (Art 243B) in section three_tiers.
Panchayati Raj is organised at the village, block and district levels; chapter teaches the three tiers (Art 243B) in section three_tiers.
73rd Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayats; chapter teaches Part IX inserted by the 73rd Amendment, w.e.f. 24-4-1993. Also mapped in POL-06.
73rd Amendment gives constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions; chapter teaches Part IX inserted by the 73rd Amendment, w.e.f. 24-4-1993. Also mapped in POL-06.
73rd Amendment allows constitutional status to the Panchayat Raj system; chapter teaches Part IX inserted by the 73rd Amendment, w.e.f. 24-4-1993. Also mapped in POL-06.
73rd Amendment is related to Panchayati Raj; chapter teaches Part IX inserted by the 73rd Amendment, w.e.f. 24-4-1993. Also mapped in POL-06.
Fundamental object of Panchayati Raj is democratic decentralisation / people's participation; chapter teaches democratic decentralisation and Gram Swaraj in section why_local.
Arunachal Pradesh is exempted from SC reservation in Panchayati Raj institutions; chapter teaches Art 243M(3A) (83rd Amendment 2000) in section powers_money.

Rajasthan adopted the three-tier Panchayati Raj system first (2 Oct 1959, Nagaur). Not taught: no verified citable source — NCERT Ch 8 (keps208.pdf) URL is unverified and the mirror text does not name Rajasthan-first; only coaching sites were found, which are not citable.

POL-21.note: Which Amendment provided constitutional status to the Panchayats? Options include both 73rd and 74th. Primary chapter POL-20 (73rd = Panchayats), but POL-21 teaches the other half of the pair: the 74th Amendment gave constitutional status to Municipalities (Part IXA, w.e.f. 1-6-1993), and the chapter's 73-vs-74 'dont_confuse' box in section why_urban_local covers exactly this discrimination.

Which constitutional amendment gives constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj institutions? Options 72nd/73rd/74th/75th. Primary chapter POL-20; POL-21 teaches that the 74th is the urban counterpart (Municipalities, Part IXA, Twelfth Schedule), so the 73/74 elimination this question demands is taught here in sections amendment_74 and why_urban_local.

Which Amendment allows a constitutional status to the Panchayat Raj system? Options 71st/72nd/73rd/74th. Primary chapter POL-20; POL-21 teaches the 74th Amendment's own subject (Municipalities) and the 73-vs-74 distinction, which is the discrimination this item tests.

The 73rd Amendment of the Constitution of India is related to which of the following? (keyed: Panchayati Raj; the 74th/Municipalities option is the distractor pair). Primary chapter POL-20; POL-21 teaches what the 74th Amendment actually relates to — Municipalities under Part IXA — in section amendment_74, covering the contrast the question is built on.

POL-22.note: Taught: the Seventh Schedule distributes legislative power between the Union and the States through the Union, State and Concurrent Lists (Art 246).
Taught: the anti-defection law came with the 52nd Amendment, 1985, which added the Tenth Schedule.
Taught: 'economic and social planning' is a Concurrent List subject in the Seventh Schedule, so both Union and States can legislate (Art 246(2)).
Taught: the 73rd Amendment gave constitutional status to Panchayati Raj institutions and added the Eleventh Schedule (Art 243G).
Taught: the 73rd Amendment allows constitutional status to the Panchayat Raj system (Eleventh Schedule).
Taught: the 73rd Amendment is related to Panchayats, not Municipalities (74th / Twelfth Schedule) — the chapter teaches the pair explicitly.

Not taught as a schedule question: the Ninth Schedule appears only as a distractor option; the question itself (Art 51, promotion of international peace) belongs to POL-05 (DPSP). The chapter does teach Art 51 in its article table, but the PYQ is mapped to POL-05 in the book's pyq_map.
Not taught as a schedule question: the Seventh Schedule appears only as a distractor option; the question itself (Welfare State ideal in the DPSP) belongs to POL-05.
